title: Histomorphometric Evaluation of Socket Preservation Healing Using Xenogeneic Bone Substitute Combined with Statin: A Prospective Split-Mouth Clinical Pilot Study
authors: Katanec, T., Šimunović, L., Likić, R., Smojver, I., Lešić, S., Pelivan, I., & Gabrić, D. (2026). Acta stomatologica Croatica, 60(2), 224–235.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The addition of locally applied simvastatin to a bovine-derived xenogeneic bone substitute did not result in significant histomorphometric differences in socket preservation after three months. At the tested dose and delivery method, simvastatin did not enhance early mineralized tissue formation compared with the bone substitute alone” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
